MAD Tygerberg

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
The Carte Blanche’s Making a Difference Trust, has delivered yet another helping hand for state hospitals and the children it services. This is MAD’s first step into the Western Cape where on the 13th April they opened a brand, spanking new, paediatric operating theatre to Tygerberg Hospital.

The MAD campaign was launched on Carte Blanche’s 20th Birthday the brainchild of Executive Producer George Mazerakis and Karolina Andropoulos – in the wake of her daughter Georgina’s passing. In George’s words instead of another negative report on the state of our hospitals why not try and do something positive he went on air promising to raise 20 million. Today 10 years later the campaign have raised money for 18 hospital projects in 10 hospitals in 6 provinces. The money they’ve raised over 120 million…and over 300 million in kind.

Tygerberg Hopital’s operating theatre is the latest hospital project….and whereas the money wasn’t the largest amount the trust had to work with the passion of individuals making this dream realised was what made every step special.

We are there at the opening of the theatre and interview Hon MEC for Health, Western Cape: Professor Nomafrench Mbambo. Other interviews take place with the donors, some of them long standing supporters of the campaign.

We profile a young child who was one of the first patients in the operating theatre, how this has made a difference to her life and her parents A heart warming story an update on Carte Blanche’s Making a Difference Campaign.

Press Release:


Making a Difference in Tygerberg
Amidst a crippling infrastructure maintenance backlog at Cape Town's Tygerberg hospital, the Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust has stepped in to help the hospital’s youngest patients. In April, the Trust with the help of its generous donors, delivered Tygerberg's first dedicated paediatric operating theatre.
In just ten years, the Campaign has raised over R130-million in funds and an estimated R300-million in kind. The funding has been entirely spent on the delivery of 18 hospital projects in 10 hospitals around the country.


Script:



Link: Tygerberg Hospital is one of the busiest in the country. More than 7 000 babies are born here every year and about a fifth of them will need surgical procedures…….

V/O
This is because Tygerberg is also the referral hospital for complex or problem pregnancies.

Derek: Hi I’m Derek.

V/O
Wendy Plaatjies has spent her days and nights this past four weeks with three month old Matteo, they are waiting for an available ICU bed for Matteo’s second surgery.

Wendy: We are like old furniture here.

V/O
Baby Matteo has Hirschmans Disease, which simply put means he does not have bowel movements …the surgery for his particular condition is extremely complex.

Wendy: He had Hirchmans disease couldn’t poo on his own when 2 weeks I came in and they said they have to do an operation.
Derek: How did you feel?
Wendy: I was scared very scared, because I don’t know about operations this is the first time here.

LINK: Tygerberg is the main referral hospital for over 50% of WC children and as you can see budgets get stretched to the limit.

Dr Dimitri  Erasmus
CEO:  Tygerberg Hospital
Dr Erasmus: Certainly the big pressure for us is the extent of the work load and that’s really driven by the burden of disease that we encounter and we have to do all of that with decreasing budgets on an annual basis...Tygerberg Hospital covers roughly about 3 million people…we also have a large referral centre for the rural areas particularly the Cape Wine lands and the West Coast In particularly Paarl and Worcester are referral regional so its quiet a big area we have to cover in terms. And we do that for all the disciplines.

V/O
And this is where Carte Blanches Making a Difference Trust has done precisely that….made a difference with a new paediatric operating theatre……. the first of it’s kind at Tygerberg.

Link : Up until now the CB MAD trust has completed 18 hospital projects around the country but this is the first step into the WC

V/O 4 sec
The trust is headed up by Karolina Andropolous.

George: 10 years ago a little girl called Georgina, Karolina’s daughter lost the fight she had cancer… she overcame cancer but died after the effects of the treatment that little girl has seen 18 hospital projects in 10 hospitals in six provinces all run by her mother.

V/O
In all the 23 years of George Mazarakis, at the helm of Carte Blanche, its this campaign he is most, proud of.

George: Karolina sat next to me at a dinner and said come and see what’s going on in the state hospitals they need help CB had reached so it was an opportunity to do something special instead of always reporting negative stories…

V/O
Today 10 years later the campaign has raised over 135 million.

Link: Up until now new borns, older babies and children had to wait in line with adults for theatre time, so you had adult trauma and emergency cases mixed with a tiny baby like this waiting for surgery, that’s all changed

Prof Daniel Sidler
Consultant Paediatric Surgeon
Tygerberg Hospital

Prof Sidler: I think we have for the first time all the necessary instrumentation treating very small babies less than a kg and obese children and we have for the first time we have everything we need.

Corné de Vos
Consultant Paediatric Surgeon
Tygerberg Hospital

Corne: So having small instruments to operate on small babies makes the procedure easier for for us Makes a Difference care is so much better.

Norman Mbazima
Chairman: Anglo American Chairman's Fund
Norman: If you go to one of these projects and you look at the operating theatre where a baby that is 500 grams is having a full operation and that will enable that baby to grow up and be like you and I those are the things that make the heart grow pitty pat.

V/O
For the donors who made this all possible, this was the first time they had seen the brand new operating theatre.

Gerard van Driel
Dräger: National Sales Manager 
Gerhard: When I walked in here it was emotional to see what they have done with the place…how neat and clean and all the technology that has been put into this theatre, benchmark, stepping stone for of the future
 
Colin Patterson
 SPAR Western Cape: Marketing Director
That technology is not freely available to this community I think it takes gives them a quantum leap in the service they can provide for these patients

Tandy Coleman
It’s just so heartwarming to see joy in surgeons faces and we are contributing to do something that makes a complete diff.

Natacha Tuna
Karl Storz Endoscopy (South Africa) 
 Portfolio Manager
 Gastroenterology, Laparoscopy and Proctology
: As I stand here I get quiet emotional, its been a long road…so I am so pleased and honoured to see it finally come to fruition.

Link: It really is amazing that this is how the new operating theatre started off, the budget was 7 million rand but it was the passion of all parties involved that saw the project through.

Raymond Visagie
THEATRE NURSE MANAGER
Visagie It was very very dirty for operations to be done in and is from a very poor quality you can see the vinyl coming off I am so glad that as a theatre manager that CB came to re furbish. The children love it when they see new colourful theatre.
Derek: They love it.
Visagie: They love it.

Up Sound Hennie …change the direction.
Hennie Theart
Unit manager clinical engineering
Clinical Engineering Department    

V/O
The brief was for sophisticated cutting edge instrumentation, and it was Tygerberg’s clinical engineering department, namely Hennie Theart and Jaques du Preez who
were responsible for getting it.

Up Sound Jacques: But its our first digital theatre as such.
 Jaques Du Preez         
Head clinical engineering
Clinical Engineering Department

Manette de Jager
Chairperson: Hospital Facility Board
Manette De Jager: This is one of my highlights of one of my 40 year career in health to be able to assure parents, that we have an upgraded theatre with best possible equipment and beautiful environment that makes such a difference.

V/O
Case In point Zunte Tinzi was born without an anus … She had just been operated on in the new theatre.

Nangamso Tinzi
It’s the first time I’m seeing her, I last saw her in ICU; I was really scared but in time she got better -after receiving treatment at Tygerberg and the doctors here were supporting ,they were always by my side- they helped.
V/O
Baby Tinzi’s operation was successful she has gone home and is doing well…. This new theatre took a lot of work and time to complete, but the returns are worth it.

Prof Sidler: if you come into a place like this your confidence goes higher it’s child friendly…it boosts the morale of the staff there is a lot of learning still to be done we still need to learn which button to press and how to manage all these instruments.

V/O
It will also be used to train other medical practioners to save lives elsewhere.

Erasmus: We are also a large training platform we focus on training specialists in all disciplines so you can imagine in field of surgery particular paediatric and orthopaedic surgery just having are registrars, specialists in training to have this equipment to learn and hone skills is really phenomenal.

V/O
Which boils down to the best possible scenario for Baby Matteo and little Tinzi.

How do you see the Future
I see a bright future, if the doctors they can fix it it’s good its right and healthy. I see a bright future

V/O
And a better future for thousands of others young lives in the Western Cape.

Tandy Coleman
 CEO : Polyflor
…saves one life a day that wasn’t saved before its paid for itself 100 times over
